title: Field Lines
tagline: Field lines and streamlines of a closed-form vector field, integrated in arclength.
method: Nothing here solves a PDE. Every field is a closed form evaluated at an array of points, so there is no lattice, no timestep, no CFL condition and nothing can diverge. Lines are traced by RK4 on `dp/ds = E/|E|` — a CONSTANT step in ARCLENGTH, not in time — with every seed advanced in lockstep and dead lines compacted out of the array. Normalising to unit speed costs one divide and buys two things: drawn line density is uniform instead of piling up wherever the field is weak, and a packet advected at speed v becomes the array index `round(v*t/ds)`, which is why the pulse module has no integrator in it at all.

output.note: Nothing in the integrator or the field kernels knows about aspect ratio — only `draw.Frame` and `RenderConfig` do. Change the resolution and the seed geometry and the same code draws a landscape plate.

modules.what: The vector fields. `coulomb` with pluggable kernel and Plummer softening, `ChargeSet` (a mutable bag of sources), `PotentialFlow` (uniform stream + doublets + vortices + sources, with exact Milne-Thomson imaging), `wires` for magnetostatics.
`trace` — RK4 in arclength, all seeds in lockstep, compacting as lines die, returning a fate code per line. Plus the seed generators and the bit-reversed fade order.
`PulseTrain` — packets that ride the lines. 103 lines with no integration in it, because a packet is just an index into the already-traced polyline.
How sources move. `WanderPath` (declared, speed-matched by measurement), `NBody` (solved — mutual Coulomb in an anisotropic well with a soft core), `keyframes`, `pulse_gate`, `smoothstep`.
`Frame` — supersampled Pillow strokes, box downsample, a bilinear density splat as a separate additive channel, then two-scale bloom. Palettes `palette_alternate`, `palette_angle`, `palette_fate`.
`RenderConfig` (resolution, fps, supersample, bloom, density), the NVENC probe, ffmpeg resolution.

objects.intro: A field is any callable `f(P) -> V` on an (N,2) array. That is the entire contract — swap the callable and not one line of the integrator, the pulses or the drawing changes.

items.name: coulomb
items.what: Point sources with `inv_sq` or `inv_r` falloff, Plummer-softened.
items.notes: `soft` is not cosmetic: without it an RK4 step that lands near a charge takes a NaN. `inv_r` changes magnitude falloff, not line shape.

items.name: ChargeSet
items.what: A mutable bag of point sources. Rebuild `pos`/`q` every frame to move charges, change their magnitude, or flip their SIGN.
items.notes: `sinks(sign=-1)` returns the positions a line may legitimately terminate on, excluding any source whose magnitude has decayed to nothing — otherwise lines snap onto an invisible marker.

items.name: PotentialFlow
items.what: Uniform stream plus doublets, point vortices and sources. `cylinder()` places an exactly-imaged body with optional bound circulation.
items.notes: One doublet per body is exact only for an ISOLATED body — two cylinders each violate the other's boundary condition (measured max|v.n| = 0.81|U|). The fix is ONE cylinder plus Milne-Thomson images of every external singularity, which is exact for arbitrary external flow: 0.81 -> 0.0005. The stream direction derives the doublet axis; it is never a free parameter.

items.name: wires
items.notes: Written and never used in a composition. It is the cheapest route to closed field lines that never terminate — the one topology electrostatics cannot make — and `END_LOOP` already reports it.

items.name: trace
items.signature: trace(fieldfn, seeds, ds=6.0, n_steps=440, sinks=None, capture_r=16.0, bounds=..., sgn=+1)
items.what: Returns `pts (N,S+1,2)`, `length (N,)` and `ended (N,)`. RK4 in arclength, lockstep over the whole seed array.
items.notes: `capture_r` must always be >= `ds`, or a line steps straight over its own sink. A per-line Python loop turns ~450 vector ops into ~90k scalar ones and costs about 50x.

items.name: END codes
items.what: How each line ended: captured by a negative source, stalled at a saddle, reached the frame margin, ran out of arclength, or closed/spiralled.
items.notes: `END_BUDGET` is a BUG, not a tuning target. It means `capture_r < ds` or the bounds are wrong. Do not raise `n_steps` to make it go away.

items.name: seed_ring
items.what: Seeds on a circle — the radial fan.

items.name: seed_rake
items.what: Seeds on a line — the inlet rake for a stream.
items.notes: A rake has to be WIDER than the frame: at a modest stream tilt a 2000 px descent drifts a streamline ~320 px sideways, so a rake that only just covers the frame leaves the downstream third black.

items.name: fade_order
items.what: Bit-reversed lighting order, so the first k seeds for ANY k are quasi-uniformly spread.
items.notes: This is what lets line count be an animation channel. Re-spacing seeds on every integer crossing of an animated N(t) makes the whole fan snap — the single most likely visual bug in this format.

items.name: PulseTrain
items.what: Beat-locked packets riding the lines, as an index range into the traced polyline.
items.notes: `stagger=0` for a radial fan — synchronous packets at equal arclength form the expanding ring that makes the format work. `stagger=1.0` for a parallel bundle, where the same packets stay collinear and sweep as a solid bar that reads as a scan artefact.

items.name: WanderPath
items.what: A declared path for a source — the rig holding a charge somewhere.
items.notes: Speed-matched by measurement, not by taste.

items.name: NBody
items.what: Sources solved under mutual Coulomb in an anisotropic well with a soft core. Nothing keyframed.
items.notes: The core must be short-range against a 1/r^2 attraction: 1/r^3 is still comparable to Coulomb at 200 px. Use 1/r^5 and size it by the ENERGY it must absorb (U(0) = core_k/(4*core_soft^4) > v^2/2), not by a force at some distance. Substeps at a fixed rate independent of fps, so a 30 fps preview and a 60 fps final are the same animation.

items.name: keyframes
items.what: Piecewise interpolation for any scalar channel.

items.name: pulse_gate
items.what: Windowed gate for turning a channel on and off.

items.name: palette_alternate
items.what: Adjacent seeds alternate between two blues.
items.notes: At high line counts these beat into a radial MOIRE. That is emergent, it is the cheapest visual interest in the format, and it is deliberate.

items.name: palette_fate
items.what: Colour by how the line ENDED — captured versus escaped.
items.notes: The colour change IS the physics. Currently used by one composition; it suits any scene with capture events at least as well.

scenes_intro: Five, and they are a deliberate spread over the properties the format can carry — one property each, no reskins. The compositions are not shipped; the list is here because what each one PROVES is reusable even when the code is not.

scenes.name: dipole_flower
scenes.what: Seed count as an animation channel, and capture as a topology EVENT. A mobile negative source toggles magnitude; above a threshold its capacity exceeds the centre's emission and it takes the entire flux — the picture snaps from a five-pole flower to a teardrop in about a second.

scenes.name: rosette_waltz
scenes.what: Continuous reconnection under MOVING sinks. Bundles are handed between sinks through null points; the rosette is never drawn, only the sinks move.

scenes.name: pair_dance
scenes.what: Nothing keyframed — the SOURCES are solved. Six charges under mutual Coulomb in an anisotropic well, launched tangentially, with lines coloured by fate.

scenes.name: charge_wave
scenes.what: MAGNITUDE and SIGN as animation channels. Seven sources in a swaying column with a travelling-wave charge; lines are born and die as sources cross zero, and marker radius reads the state out honestly.

scenes.name: stream_glass
scenes.what: KERNEL GENERALITY — the reuse proof. Potential flow: a tilting stream, one exactly-imaged cylinder with swinging bound circulation, two free vortices orbiting it. Not one line of the integrator, the pulses or the drawing changes; only the callable.

parameters_intro: Density is the content here — the biggest lever by a wide margin is how many lines are lit and how that number moves over the clip.

parameters.name: n_slots / N(t)
parameters.meaning: How many seeds exist, and how many are lit at time t. The whole arc of this format is a build and a drop in line count.

parameters.name: ds
parameters.meaning: Arclength step. Sets drawn line resolution and the index scale that packets ride.

parameters.name: capture_r
parameters.meaning: How close a line must come to a sink to be captured.

parameters.name: s_max / n_steps
parameters.range: Must clear a straight bounds traverse WITH SLACK. 2795 px allowed for a 2130 px straight run left 34% of lines out of budget as soon as they meandered.

parameters.name: glow_mul / glow2_mul
parameters.range: There is no single right exposure for a radial fan and a parallel bundle. 210 near-parallel lines cover a third of the frame, and a wide halo over that integrates to a flat field with no contrast anywhere.

parameters.name: dens_gain / dens_ref
parameters.meaning: The additive density channel — what blows a converging core to white.

parameters.name: line_width
parameters.range: Use EVEN world widths. Pillow rounds stroke widths to integers, so 1.7 becomes 2 px at preview and 3 px at final — the final comes out 25% finer and darker than the preview promised.

parameters.name: period
parameters.range: 2.5 s is one 4/4 bar at 96 BPM
